title: Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 — Executive summary
key_claim: Export controls have driven a sharp price divergence between Chinese and other markets: European prices for gallium and heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) are around five times Chinese domestic prices, and germanium almost three times.
frame_summary: Argues that export controls have converted supply-concentration risk from a theoretical vulnerability into an immediate economic-security problem, and that diversification carries a 'mineral security premium' governments should treat as insurance worth paying, including through price-based mechanisms.
verbatim_quote: In Europe, prices for gallium and heavy rare earths (dysprosium and terbium) are currently around five times higher than Chinese domestic prices, and germanium prices are almost three times higher
verbatim_list: The number of mineral tariff codes subject to Chinese export controls has tripled since 2023.

Although the expanded measures were suspended for one year until November 2026, the vulnerabilities remain. Their full implementation could put an estimated USD 6.5 trillion per year of downstream production outside China at risk across the automotive, high-tech, defence and energy sectors.
The additional cost of supply diversification can be viewed as a mineral security premium
diversifying magnet rare earth supply chains would require around USD 60 billion of investment over the next decade

title: G7 Leaders' Declaration on Securing Supply Chains for Critical Minerals, Evian
date_evidence: Date: 17/06/2026G7 Leaders' Declaration on securing supply chains for critical minerals
key_claim: G7 leaders committed to reduce dependence on a single non-G7 supplier of rare earths and permanent magnets to under 60% by 2030 and said they continue to explore measures including revenue stabilisation mechanisms, price-gap subsidies, joint procurement, quotas and price floors.
frame_summary: Frames critical-minerals dependence as economic coercion to be countered collectively, committing the G7 to a managed-market toolkit of targets, stockpiles, traceability and possible price instruments rather than to restoring a single open market.
verbatim_quote: We also continue to explore demand and supply-side measures such as diversification requirements, revenue stabilization mechanisms including price-gap subsidies, joint procurement instruments and trade-related instruments such as quotas and price floors.
verbatim_list: we aim to significantly reduce our dependencies on a single supplier outside the G7 and partner countries for rare earths and permanent magnets to under 60 per cent by 2030 and continuing to decrease further over time, with an ambition to reach 50 per cent as soon as possible

title: USA Rare Earth, Inc. — Exhibit 99.1: Completion of Upsized $1.55 Billion Capitalization of the U.S. Government-Backed SPV for Serra Verde Offtake
date_evidence: STILLWATER, Okla., August 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- USA Rare Earth, Inc.
key_claim: A US-government-backed SPV completed a $1.55 billion capitalisation, including a $750 million Department of War investment and a forward purchase contract of not less than $300 million over five years, to buy 100% of Serra Verde's Phase 1 magnetic rare earth output under a 15-year offtake with guaranteed price floors.
frame_summary: Presents state-backed capital, take-or-pay offtake and guaranteed price floors as the mechanism for building a Western mine-to-magnet chain, celebrating the industry's first heavy rare earth floors as strategic infrastructure.
verbatim_quote: On the same day, Serra Verde announced it entered into a 15-year offtake agreement to supply the SPV capitalized by various U.S. Government agencies, as well as private capital sources for 100% of its Phase I production with guaranteed price floors for its magnetic rare earths, including the industry’s first and only price floors for heavy rare earths dysprosium and terbium.
verbatim_list: Pursuant to the capitalization transaction, totaling an upsized $1.55 billion in funding
The U.S. government has entered into a forward purchase contract with the SPV for the purchase of not less than $300 million of rare earth payable products over five years.
The Department of War has committed to a $750 million investment in the SPV - $250 million more than the $500 million originally contemplated under the Offtake Agreement.

title: Rare Earth Export Restrictions One Year Later
key_claim: Washington's response to China's export controls includes the $400 million MP Materials equity deal with a 10-year price floor of $110 per kilogram for neodymium-praseodymium, a Lynas offtake at the same floor, and a February 2026 US-Japan action plan to work toward border-adjusted price floors.
frame_summary: Argues the US has moved from ad hoc emergency responses to a deliberate market-shaping industrial policy for rare earths, using price floors, offtakes and allied frameworks, while remaining far from genuine supply resilience.
verbatim_quote: The deal included a 10-year price floor of $110 per kilogram for MP Materials’ neodymium-praseodymium output, helping shield the company from depressed prices driven by Chinese overproduction.

while using price floors to stabilize revenues and incentivize private sector investment. Together, these measures reflect a more comprehensive market-shaping approach to building resilient and commercially viable rare earth supply chains.

title: Pentagon locks in $1.55B rare earth deal
key_claim: The Serra Verde offtake sets minimum prices of $2,050/kg for terbium, $575/kg for dysprosium and $110/kg for neodymium and praseodymium, escalating 2% annually, with Serra Verde keeping 70% of any excess of market prices over the floor.

title: Japan seeks G7 price floors to break China's rare earth grip
key_claim: Japan is pushing the G7 to adopt a floor-price guarantee system for critical-mineral contracts, with the $110/kg Lynas-JARE floor seen as the reference point for neodymium-praseodymium in any broader G7 arrangement.
frame_summary: Argues Japan has learned from its 2010 rare earth shock and is now assembling a coalition-based price-guarantee strategy, while Chinese commentary dismisses allied projects as uneconomic and doomed by cost and capacity gaps.
verbatim_quote: What Tokyo is now pushing the G7 to adopt is a floor-price guarantee system for critical-mineral contracts, with each mineral carrying its own agreed-upon minimum price.
